messages:
maria: heads up — us-west2a showing ~30% GPU pending on packer-node pools for the last hour. most pending pods are tiny inference shards from tenant-beta, but they can't binpack because of the tenant-isolation slope heuristic we rolled earlier.

devin: looking at the graph now. I can reproduce pending spike + many 0.1 GPU pods stuck in Pending

sre-bot: ALERT: scheduler_pending_pods_high (us-west2a) — 82 pods pending, avg wait 4.2m — link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/pack/west2a

omited: quick note — network probes to rack-12 had transient loss 2x between 23:10-23:14 which delayed kubelet heartbeat and kept some nodes from accepting late-bind. could contribute.

oliver: hmm — two separate factors then: (1) tenant-affinity weight too strict (slope prevents cross-tenant packing), (2) short network blips preventing latebind warmpool fills.

maria: short-term fix ideas: 1) lower tenant-affinity weight to allow best-effort co-located tiny pods, 2) temporarily relax the "slope" for tiny-pod class, 3) manual small-pod eviction to reseed warmpool. any objections?

devin: agree lower weight is safest. can put a canary in us-west2a only and monitor eviction/repack rates. i'd rather avoid manual evictions if we can adjust policy.

feng: cost note — if we allow more cross-tenant co-locates we might increase tail latency for large reserved pools; we should limit change to pods <0.25 GPU and set a short trial window. also watch EBS iops on those hosts.

maria: plan then: devin will deploy a scheduler config canary that reduces tenant_affinity_weight from 120 -> 40 only for tiny-pod class, expires in 2h; oliver will throttle latebind timeout probe to 10s to avoid flapping false-negatives; i will monitor pending count and p99 latency.

devin: will deploy canary 23:45 PST. ps — kubectl to watch:
```
kubectl -n kube-system get configmap scheduler-config -o yaml | sed -n '1,200p'
# then apply patch with: kubectl apply -f scheduler-canary-usw2a.yaml
```

sre-bot: INC-2026-042 created for tracking. assignees: devin, maria.

maria: if canary looks good we'll roll region-wide but keep threshold <0.25 GPU for 24h. i'll post results in this thread in 30/60/120 mins. :thumbsup:

oliver: small follow-up — can we add a telemetry tag to show tenant-affinity matches per-node (so we can roll back quickly if mixing increases tail lat)? simple prometheus label should do it.

devin: yup adding a meter in the canary now. will report back after first 15m.

maria: thanks team — leaning on canary metrics now.
